WA-2025-HB1069.s: This law lets the employer bargain with Department of Corrections employees over contributions for supplemental retirement benefits, including medical plans, that are run by or for an employee organization. It says these contributions are a required subject of bargaining. It also says they are not part of interest arbitration as an impasse procedure.

WA-2025-HB1128.s: This law creates a Washington child care workforce standards board with members from child care workers, employers, a training program, parents, and two state agencies. The board must meet quarterly, hold public hearings, gather data, and make recommendations to improve child care worker employment standards. It can recommend statewide standards and standards for specific jobs or regions, but not rules about licensing child care facilities. It affects child care workers and child care employers.

WA-2025-HB1155.s: The law changes rules on noncompete deals, which are agreements that can limit someone’s work after a job ends. It makes these agreements void, expands what counts as a noncompete, and limits some business limits in nonsolicit agreements, including some patient-related deals in health care. Employers must give written notice to certain workers by October 1, 2027, and people or the state can sue for damages and fees. It becomes effective on June 30, 2027.
WA-2025-HB1155.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (1155-S.E SBR LC TA 26, 2026-02-24)

WA-2025-HB1170.s: The law requires certain covered providers to include provenance data in some video, image, and audio content that is created or materially altered by generative artificial intelligence, when commercially and technically reasonable. It also requires government agencies that use an artificial intelligence system to interact with consumers to disclose that before or during the interaction. The law limits when it applies and says only the attorney general may bring certain enforcement actions.

WA-2025-HB1187.s: The law bars ambulance services from sending accident-related medical debt to a collection agency until 120 days after the first bill is sent. It covers motor vehicle crashes, including when a pedestrian or bicyclist is hit by a vehicle. If an ambulance service has a pattern of unresolved billing or notice violations, state officials may review it and may fine it or take other allowed action. It takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB1187.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (1187-S.E HBR PL 26, 2026-03-13)

WA-2025-HB1210.s: The law changes a property tax break for clean energy transformation business facilities in targeted urban areas. After a project is done, the owner must give the city proof that key wage, job, and labor agreement rules were met, and the city must check some of those labor standards with the state labor agency. Cities may also give these projects up to four more years to finish, and the law takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB1210.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (1210-S.E2 HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-HB1295.s: The law requires new early reading and writing materials for kindergarten through grade 4 to include key parts of literacy, such as reading fluency, vocabulary, phonological awareness, and oral language. It also says these materials must fit student needs, match state reading standards, and line up with teacher literacy skills standards. The state will also update teacher training and support on dyslexia for students in kindergarten through grade 4, with some reporting changed to every two years.
WA-2025-HB1295.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (1295-S.E HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-16)

WA-2025-HB1302.s: Municipal utilities in Washington may create local programs to waive connection charges for properties owned or developed by groups using the property for industrial symbiosis. That means organizations working together on projects that measurably cut resource use or greenhouse gas emissions.
WA-2025-HB1302.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (1302-S HBR PL 26, 2026-03-12)

WA-2025-HB1345.s: This law sets limits for detached accessory dwelling units outside urban growth areas in counties that plan under this chapter. It says counties may allow them only if the parcel meets water, sewage, size, driveway, and distance rules, and if the parcel is not split to avoid the limits. It also requires counties to track permits, report them each year, and add code enforcement measures for unpermitted units.

WA-2025-HB1376.s: People who pay Washington capital gains tax could pay it up to six months before it is due. If they later overpay for that tax period and get money back, no interest would be charged for the early payment period. It became law and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB1376.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (1376 HBR APH 26, 2026-01-15)

WA-2025-HB1390.s: The bill ends the community protection program on January 1, 2026. It also lets Developmental Disabilities Administration clients in that program get less restrictive service options. By December 31, 2025, the agency must make and carry out a plan to move everyone in the program to other services or programs.
WA-2025-HB1390.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (1390-S SBR HS TA 25, 2025-03-29)

WA-2025-HB1408.s: The law sets aside part of state sales tax money from certain large sports and event facilities for community preservation and development authorities, or CPDAs. The money goes into a CPDA account and is split evenly between daily costs and capital needs, like buildings and major projects. It also requires a state review by December 1, 2034, and CPDAs to send reports every two years on their plans, spending, and community impact. The law took effect on March 25, 2026, and ends on January 1, 2037.
WA-2025-HB1408.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (1408-S.E SBR APS2 26, 2026-03-12)

WA-2025-HB1500.s: Changes what must be in a resale certificate for a unit in a common interest community. It would require the most recent audit report, current board rules and resolutions, and the latest reserve study, and it would limit what an association can charge for making the certificate. It also sets rules for rush and update fees, bars some third-party payment setup demands, and lets a unit owner sue over missing, late, or wrong certificate information.
WA-2025-HB1500.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (1500-S.E HBR APH 26, 2026-01-16)

WA-2025-HB1501.s: This law requires associations in common interest communities to answer written certified-mail inquiries from owners about governance or operations within 30 days. The association can extend the deadline for board review, a complex inquiry, or to get a legal or other third-party opinion, and it must treat those opinion costs as a common expense. The law also allows the association to set reasonable rules on how often it must respond, and parts of the law expire on January 1, 2028.

WA-2025-HB1526.s: Retailers with a snack bar liquor license may also sell wine by the glass for people to drink on the premises. The law takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB1526.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (1526 HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-HB1570.s: The law adds some non-academic student jobs at Western Washington University to the state rules for collective bargaining, which means students in those jobs can negotiate certain work terms together. It covers listed roles such as resident advisors, customer service representatives, and event assistants, and it leaves out certain higher-level and confidential employees. The bargaining rules do not cover academic rules, class sizes, or the base tuition and fee amounts, and any pay terms must stay within limits set by the Legislature. It became law on March 18, 2026.
WA-2025-HB1570.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (1570-S SBR LC OC 26, 2026-02-24)

WA-2025-HB1634.s: This law requires the Office of the Superintendent of Public Instruction and educational service districts to work with other agencies and community partners to create a technical assistance and training framework for school behavioral health support. The framework is meant to help school districts and public schools with prevention, early identification, early intervention, and crisis intervention, including finding resources, funding, and community-based services. It also says schools and districts must keep following existing student behavioral health duties while the framework is being developed. The office must give the legislature an update on the framework by November 1, 2027.

WA-2025-HB1701.s: Allows more than one liquor licensee to run separate spaces in the same facility, and lets the facility owner lease space or a kitchen to other licensees or businesses. It also lets certain alcohol makers operate in the same facility as a retail liquor licensee, as long as each keeps its own space and all needed permits and licenses. The law was signed and takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB1701.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (1701-S2 SBR LC TA 26, 2026-02-22)

WA-2025-HB1710.s: This law sets rules for certain local governments called "covered jurisdictions" under the Washington voting rights act of 2018. Before a covered jurisdiction can adopt or carry out a covered policy, it must submit it to the attorney general and get a certificate of no objection, and the policy is not effective until that happens. The attorney general must also keep a public website with a list of covered jurisdictions and the status of submitted policies. The law also allows court actions by the attorney general or an aggrieved person in certain cases.

WA-2025-HB1750.s: The law updates Washington’s Voting Rights Act rules on claims about vote suppression and vote dilution. It sets a new test for when an election rule or action by a local government would burden the voting rights of a protected group, and it changes some court standards and remedies for those cases. It became law as Chapter 215, 2026 Laws, and takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB1750.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (1750-S2.E HBR PL 26, 2026-03-17)

WA-2025-HB1795.s: The law limits when school staff and other providers of public educational services may use restraint or isolation on students. It bars certain kinds of restraint, sets stricter rules for student plans, and stops schools from setting up new rooms mainly for isolation. It also requires state report summaries to be published in a way that allows trend analysis, and it applies these rules to more than just school districts.
WA-2025-HB1795.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (1795-S.E HBR PL 26, 2026-03-20)

WA-2025-HB1796.s: This law changes when school districts can borrow money for school construction without a vote of district electors. For some school construction projects, the district must have voter-approved levy support, must not have been on binding conditions in the prior three years, and must agree to delay state financial assistance for two years. It also requires public notice and a hearing before issuing nonvoted bonds over $250,000, except for refinancing or refunding existing bonds.

WA-2025-HB1903.s: This law establishes a statewide low-income energy assistance program within the department of commerce. It is meant to reduce energy burden for low-income households in Washington by sending funds to participating utilities, which must pass the assistance on to eligible residential customers and show it on monthly bills. The department must make rules for enrollment, including in-person, online, and phone applications, and the rules may allow self-attestation, verification of income, and auto enrollment of known eligible households. Electric utilities must also keep their low-income energy assistance from being reduced because of this program.

WA-2025-HB1906.s: The law adds notice rules for water system ownership changes. Public water systems and water companies must tell customers and nearby local water providers before a sale or transfer, and the state utility regulator must use set rules when it reviews water rates and ownership deals.
WA-2025-HB1906.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (1906-S2 SBR ENET OC 26, 2026-02-25)

WA-2025-HB1909.s: This law creates a court unification task force to study Washington’s court system and look at ways to make court operations more unified and consistent. The task force includes lawmakers, city and county representatives, court officials, lawyers, and people with lived experience in civil court and as a formerly incarcerated person. It must hold its first meeting by October 1, 2026, and submit a preliminary report by June 30, 2027 and a final report by June 30, 2028. The task force expires on December 31, 2029.

WA-2025-HB1916.s: The law changes how voter registration challenges are filed and reviewed in Washington. It limits the kinds of records a challenger can use, requires more specific forms and signed papers, and gives county auditors more steps to check a challenge before a hearing. It also changes who can run the hearing, what proof is needed, and adds penalties for knowingly giving false information. It takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB1916.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (1916-S.E SBA SGTE 26, 2026-02-15)

WA-2025-HB1941.s: Licensed cannabis producers may form agricultural associations, such as cooperatives, to work together on business tasks. These groups may process, handle, and market their products together. For this purpose, cannabis is treated as an agricultural product, and the law takes effect June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB1941.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (1941 HBA AGNR 25, 2025-02-17)

WA-2025-HB1960.s: The law changes taxes for some solar and wind projects in Washington. Starting in 2027, certain equipment used to make or store renewable energy at large qualifying facilities would be exempt from property tax, and a new annual renewable energy excise tax would apply to qualifying solar and wind systems based on their size, age, and type. It also changes how local tax limits are figured for wind and solar facility growth, and it takes effect on January 1, 2028.
WA-2025-HB1960.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (1960 HBA FIN 26, 2026-01-22)

WA-2025-HB1974.s: The law lets a public corporation, public housing authority, or nonprofit act as a land bank to buy, hold, improve, lease, or sell land for affordable housing. It sets rules for keeping housing affordable, such as 30-year limits on at least half of the land or homes sold or leased, and it requires yearly public reports on land held and transferred. Counties must give land banks first chance to buy tax-foreclosed property, and the law took effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB1974.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (1974 HBR HOUS 26, 2026-01-23)

WA-2025-HB1980.s: In counties with more than 2 million people, local officials may approve two-year pilot programs that let some private employer transportation services use certain transit lanes, with the public transit provider's approval. The plan must set rules for how these lanes are used, how the program is watched and enforced, and how results are reported each year. Fee money must cover the local cost to run the permit program, and any extra money must go to maintaining and improving the transit lanes. It became law and takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB1980.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (1980-S.E HBR PL 26, 2026-03-12)

WA-2025-HB1983.s: The law expands the tax rule for timberland to cover some forest land sold or transferred to a government body. To get the 1.28 percent real estate excise tax rate, the government body must keep managing the land as forest or timber land and give the county assessor a timber plan or a notice that it will do so. It became law and takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB1983.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (1983 HBR PL 26, 2026-03-10)

WA-2025-HB2034.s: The law changes how Washington’s police and firefighter retirement plan 1 is handled. It ends that plan on June 30, 2029, creates a restated version, and keeps benefits the same for people already getting payments. Some active members on February 1, 2025, may choose to start annuity payments early, get five extra years of service credit, and receive a one-time $25,000 payment if they make that choice by January 1, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2034.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2034 HBR APP 25, 2025-04-07)

WA-2025-HB2089.s: The law changes how certain large mortgage lenders are taxed on interest from loans backed by homes. It applies to high volume mortgage lenders and removes a rule that they had to be based in 10 or more states. Starting in 2027, state officials must estimate the added tax money and move that amount into a wildfire response and forest restoration fund.
WA-2025-HB2089.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2089-S HBR PL 26, 2026-03-12)

WA-2025-HB2091.s: Public employers covered by the state’s public service labor law would have to give certain employee contact information to the workers’ exclusive union representative. The rule is extended to all employers covered by that law. It became law on March 24, 2026, and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2091.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2091 SBR LC TA 26, 2026-02-20)

WA-2025-HB2104.s: This law makes the Aviation Assurance Funding Program permanent by removing its end date. It affects funding for aviation help in response to wildland fires and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2104.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2104 HBR PL 26, 2026-03-10)

WA-2025-HB2105.s: The law requires employers to give workers and their representatives notice within five days if the employer gets a federal notice of inspection of Form I-9 records or the results of that inspection. The notices must include certain details in English and in the five most used non-English languages in Washington, and the state Attorney General must publish a model notice by September 1, 2026. It takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2105.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2105-S2 HBR PL 26, 2026-03-31)

WA-2025-HB2110.s: The law lets a registered nurse without EMT certification help with certain ambulance transfers between medical facilities if an EMT is in the ambulance, the nurse is trained for the patient’s needs, and no paramedic or nurse with EMT certification is available. That nurse must follow the doctor’s medical direction and stay within the nurse’s normal scope of practice. The hospital sending the patient must work with the ambulance service to make sure the nurse knows the ambulance equipment and supplies. It became law and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2110.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2110-S.E HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-HB2114.s: Washington now lets a person ask for a free replacement of a defective license plate for the same vehicle if they apply within 24 months of issuance. The Department of Licensing may waive the replacement cost for requests made after 24 months and up to five years after issuance. The law also sets when a plate can be replaced and when the department does not have to provide a new one. It takes effect on 1/1/2027.
WA-2025-HB2114.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2114-S SBA TRAN 26, 2026-02-22)

WA-2025-HB2124.s: The state pension office may turn some small monthly retirement payments from PERS, TRS, SERS, PSERS, and LEOFF into one lump-sum payment instead of paying each month. The monthly amount that can be changed from $50 to $250, and that amount can rise each year as the retirement director decides. It became law and takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2124.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2124 HBR PL 26, 2026-03-10)

WA-2025-HB2156.s: This law requires the attorney general to designate some investigator positions as limited authority Washington peace officers. These investigators may investigate economic and financial crimes, but they do not have the power to detain or arrest anyone and may not be armed. They may serve search warrants only by electronic service on a business after a judicial officer approves the warrant, and they must meet training and criminal background check requirements. The law does not change the investigative authority or criminal jurisdiction of other law enforcement agencies.

WA-2025-HB2165.s: The law makes false identification as a peace officer a gross misdemeanor, which is a less serious crime. It covers making, showing, or having items, including vehicles, that use police or similar agency markings to make someone seem like a peace officer when they are not. It also covers falsely claiming to be a peace officer, with some stated exceptions for certain retired officers and items kept to remember a deceased officer. It became law on March 19, 2026, and takes effect June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2165.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2165-S.E SBR LAW TA 26, 2026-02-20)

WA-2025-HB2178.s: The law changes several court deadlines and payment rules. It gives people more time to file and answer a notice of infraction, and courts must dismiss late notices. It also raises the damage amount for certain malicious mischief cases, and changes who sends out grants for collecting legal financial obligations. It became law and takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2178.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2178-S HBR PL 26, 2026-03-12)

WA-2025-HB2179.s: This law changes who can be a member of the public employees' retirement system for some port district workers. It says a port district employee is not eligible for this retirement system for any period of service covered by a federal retirement system. It also says employees covered by a private Taft-Hartley defined benefit pension plan are exempt from this retirement system for the service covered by that plan.

WA-2025-HB2192.s: The law expands the Washington traffic safety commission’s role in studying deadly crashes and the risk factors behind them. It lets the commission collect crash, toxicology, and driver license records, review deaths of pedestrians and bicyclists, and make reports and safety recommendations, with some health data kept private. It takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2192.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2192-S.E HBR PL 26, 2026-03-10)

WA-2025-HB2211.s: The law sets rules for medically tailored meals, which are fresh or frozen meals made by a qualified medical professional for a person's health condition. If state health agencies hire vendors for these meals through medical assistance programs, they must use Washington-based nonprofit groups when possible and make sure the meals match the client’s nutrition plan, allergies, and cultural needs. The meals must also meet set nutrition standards and provide enough calories, carbs, and protein. It takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2211.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2211 HBR HCW 26, 2026-01-26)

WA-2025-HB2215.s: This law changes who has climate commitment act compliance obligations for fuels supplied, produced, imported, delivered, or sold into Washington. It sets rules for when fuel suppliers, natural gas suppliers, electricity importers, waste-to-energy facilities, and railroad companies become covered entities, and it lets the department adjust some fuel thresholds by rule. It also keeps or creates exemptions for some emissions, including aviation fuels, certain watercraft fuels, biomass and biofuels, some farm fuel use, national security facilities, and municipal solid waste landfills. The governor approved the bill with one section vetoed, and it takes effect June 11, 2026.

WA-2025-HB2219.s: This law changes child care licensing rules in Washington. It keeps a single set of licensing standards for child care and early childhood programs, and it lets child care centers use limited mixed-ratio time if the youngest child’s ratio and group size are kept. It also requires private schools with early learning programs that do not receive state subsidy payments to meet certain health and safety standards, and it waives a required orientation in some cases for people who already completed it.

WA-2025-HB2225.s: This law sets rules for artificial intelligence companion chatbots in Washington. Operators must clearly say the chatbot is artificial, repeat that notice during longer chats, and stop the chatbot from claiming to be human. If the operator knows a user is a minor, or the chatbot is directed to minors, it must also block sexually explicit content, limit manipulative emotional tactics, and give the notice more often. Operators must also keep a protocol for detecting and responding to suicidal ideation or self-harm and publicly disclose details of that protocol.

WA-2025-HB2229.s: The law changes rules for Washington’s board that handles engineer and land surveyor licenses. It removes the U.S. citizenship rule for board members, requires recent work experience in Washington, and changes how temporary board members are chosen and used. It also changes some license rules, including what counts as qualifying experience and what address is listed in the public roster. It became law and takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2229.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2229-S.E HBR PL 26, 2026-03-10)

WA-2025-HB2238.s: The law requires the Washington State Department of Agriculture to track food system performance and work with other agencies, tribes, nonprofits, researchers, and industry experts on food access and farm resilience. It also directs the department to write a statewide food security plan that looks at food access, farm strength, and supply chain strength, and to give that plan to lawmakers by December 1, 2027. Starting June 30, 2030, the department must also report every four years on how Washington’s rules compare with other states for key crops. The bill became law in 2026 and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2238.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2238-S.E HBR PL 26, 2026-03-10)

WA-2025-HB2239.s: This law creates a process for a person to designate part of land they own as a family burial ground for interment of human remains. If land is co-owned, all co-owners must give written consent, and the burial ground must meet setback and size limits. It also sets rules for mausoleums and columbaria, reporting and disclosure requirements, and allows cities and counties to regulate or prohibit family burial grounds.

WA-2025-HB2247.s: This law changes the rules for veterinarian-client-patient relationships in Washington. It sets when a relationship exists, when veterinarians may use telehealth or telemedicine, and when in-person exams are needed. It also sets rules for prescriptions, records, consent, and care for commercial animal operations. The law takes effect on July 1, 2027.

WA-2025-HB2248.s: The law changes how the secretary of state handles business and charity filings, including when filings are marked as received and processed. It requires some new reports for certain new Washington entities, changes rules for some foreign entities and trademark transfers, and sets a process to restore some exchange visitor group registrations. It also limits when the secretary of state can certify a notary's signature on certain documents.
WA-2025-HB2248.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2248-S HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-HB2249.s: The law adds Washington Technology Solutions officers and employees who do network and system security work to the state civil service rules. These workers are now covered by the State Civil Service Law. It became law in 2026 and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2249.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2249 HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-20)

WA-2025-HB2251.s: This bill creates a climate commitment act operating account and a climate commitment act capital account in the state treasury. Money from the auction of allowances would be deposited into these accounts and could be spent only after appropriation. The money could be used for many climate-related projects, including clean water, healthy forests, electric vehicles, energy efficiency, and help for tribal projects and affected fossil fuel workers. It also sets limits on how the money can be used and requires some projects to meet high labor standards.

WA-2025-HB2254.s: The law lets certain reasonable costs for the third-party administrator be included when figuring the health care assessment for health carriers, self-funded multiple employer welfare arrangements, and employers or other groups that provide health care in Washington. It does not allow the state health agency’s other admin costs for these programs to be added to the assessment. It became law as Chapter 58, 2026 Laws, and takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2254.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2254 SBA WM 26, 2026-02-18)

WA-2025-HB2264.s: The law changes how workers can keep unemployment benefits when they leave under an employer layoff or workforce cutback plan. Starting on June 14, 2026, the employer only has to end the worker’s job because of that plan, and the employer may let the worker take back an offer without losing benefits. It applies to unemployment claims filed on or after that date.
WA-2025-HB2264.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2264 HBR PL 26, 2026-03-12)

WA-2025-HB2266.s: This law changes city and county zoning and permitting rules for permanent supportive housing, transitional housing, indoor emergency housing, and indoor emergency shelters. In urban growth areas, cities and counties must allow these housing types in certain zones and cannot require stricter standards than those for other lodging or residential development in the same zone. For indoor emergency shelters and indoor emergency housing, it allows some written certifications and, in some cases, talks about added health and safety requirements when they are near another shelter or a school.

WA-2025-HB2274.s: The law changes Washington rules for commercial email and text messages. For a subject line to count as false or misleading, the sender must have actual knowledge, or knowledge shown by clear facts, that it is false or misleading. It also lowers set damages for a banned commercial email or text to $100, or actual damages if higher, and applies to cases filed on or after June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2274.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2274-S.E HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-HB2296.s: The law requires electric utilities to let customers install one customer-owned meter-mounted device between the meter and meter socket if the device and installation meet set safety and approval rules. Utilities must review device requests within 90 days for larger utilities and 180 days for smaller ones, post approval choices online, and may charge customers for related service work; cities and counties may not ban these devices. Utilities must follow the new rules within 6 months after the law takes effect, and the law takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2296.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2296-S HBR APH 26, 2026-02-11)

WA-2025-HB2309.s: Washington state law now bars the state job classification plan from making a postgraduate degree the only way to show you qualify for a job, unless that degree is required by law. It affects people applying for state jobs and state hiring rules. The law takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2309.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2309 SBR APS 26, 2026-03-04)

WA-2025-HB2317.s: This law changes Washington’s child care licensing rules by exempting certain school-day early childhood education and assistance programs and Head Start programs from being treated as an "agency." The exemption applies when those programs are in a public school building or a community or technical college building, or on the premises of a public school or community or technical college.

WA-2025-HB2320.s: This law changes Washington’s firearms rules for manufacturing that uses three-dimensional printers, CNC milling machines, or digital firearm manufacturing code. It amends several firearms law definitions, including “firearm,” “frame or receiver,” “assault weapon,” and “large capacity magazine.” It affects people and businesses involved in making, importing, or distributing firearms and related parts in Washington.

WA-2025-HB2323.s: The Department of Licensing must set up a Blue Envelope Program to help with communication during traffic stops for people who are neurodiverse. Free blue envelopes must be available at driver licensing offices and include safety tips, guidance for officers, and what papers to keep inside, like registration and proof of insurance. The department must also keep program information and resources on a website. It became law and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2323.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2323-S HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-HB2325.s: Creates a tourism assessment program that lets a state tourism group charge eligible businesses a yearly fee based on a share of gross revenue, after the businesses in each industry sector approve it. The money would fund statewide tourism promotion, and the program would be guided by a ratepayer oversight board made up of business and tourism representatives. It also changes the tourism authority’s board, requires annual budgets and reports, and became law with an effective date of June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2325.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2325-S2.E HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-28)

WA-2025-HB2334.s: This law allows in-person cash transactions to be rounded to the nearest five-cent increment when pennies are not used. It applies only to cash paid in person, not to electronic payments, cards, money orders, or other noncash methods, and a customer can still pay the exact total if they have exact legal tender. It says rounding does not change the sales price, taxes owed or collected, or fees, and local governments may not block the rounding allowed by the law.

WA-2025-HB2338.s: The law lets weatherization grant money and matching funds pay for larger neighborhood-based weatherization projects with multiple homes. These projects can include partial or full weatherization, energy-saving work, or basic repairs, and they are not limited to homes where every unit is low-income, though low-income households must be given priority. The state agency in charge may also make rules to run the program.
WA-2025-HB2338.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2338 HBR PL 26, 2026-03-12)

WA-2025-HB2339.s: The law changes how some nursing titles may be used in Washington. It lets advanced registered nurse practitioners use the titles ARNP or APRN, and lets each nurse type use its own title and short form; people without an ARNP license may not use those titles. It also lets certain nurse anesthetists keep giving controlled substances under set rules, removes the need to send nursing school transcripts with some license applications, and lets the board issue interim permits while exam results are pending. It became law and takes effect June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2339.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2339-S HBR PL 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-HB2340.s: The law adds nursing assistants to the group of workers who can get a stipend to help pay for a substance use disorder monitoring program. It also limits when the Department of Health and the Board can post an enforcement action against a nursing assistant on a public website if the assistant contacted and, if advised, joined a Board-approved monitoring program and has mostly followed the order or agreement. It took effect on July 1, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2340.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2340 SBR APS 26, 2026-03-04)

WA-2025-HB2348.s: The law changes how the state land agency, DNR, must tell the public about land sales. It moves sale notices and land lists to DNR’s website and no longer requires some paper postings or pamphlets. It also says certain lands may be sold only after appraisal, for at least fair market value, and if the sale is in the state’s or a trust’s best interest. It took effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2348.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2348 SBR APS 26, 2026-03-04)

WA-2025-HB2350.s: This law requires the state agency to give quick notice when a residential habilitation center is found out of line with federal care rules. The notice must explain the problem in plain words, any fix plan, and later steps on whether the facility is back in compliance, and it must be posted where residents, visitors, and people asking about placement can see it. The notice must also be sent to certain other people by writing or email, and in English or a requested alternative language. It became law and takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2350.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2350-S SBA HS 26, 2026-02-17)

WA-2025-HB2353.s: The law raises the dollar cutoff for certain state building projects that need extra planning review from $10 million to $15 million. After that, the state budget office must update the cutoff each year for inflation, starting July 1, 2027. It took effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2353.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2353 HBR PL 26, 2026-03-10)

WA-2025-HB2354.s: The law updates rules for common interest communities, which are groups like condos and planned neighborhoods that share some property and costs. It changes how costs are handled for electric vehicle chargers and heat pumps, gives some small middle-housing communities a break from most state rules, and raises the audit trigger from $50,000 to $100,000. It also changes when a community can qualify for a small-community exemption and when some communities must prepare reserve studies.
WA-2025-HB2354.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2354-S SBR APS 26, 2026-03-05)

WA-2025-HB2360.s: The law lets public and private schools keep albuterol on hand for students starting with the 2027-28 school year. It sets rules for when school nurses or trained staff can give it, and it also lets some non-nurse staff opt out in writing if they do not want that task in their job. It gives some legal protection to health workers and school staff who follow the rules. The law takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2360.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2360-S HBR APH 26, 2026-02-12)

WA-2025-HB2384.s: This law adds a new review step for some continuing care retirement community applicants that offer life care contracts. Starting July 1, 2027, they must submit an actuarial analysis, which is a financial check done by a qualified actuary, to show they can meet their contract promises. The state will review the analysis before registration is issued, and the public online list of registered communities must link to the review results.
WA-2025-HB2384.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2384-S2 HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-20)

WA-2025-HB2385.s: The law changes Washington’s Medicaid access program and requires the Health Care Authority to send needed state plan changes or waiver requests to the federal government by September 1, 2030. It would raise payment rates for certain medical services, including anesthesia, emergency room care, surgery, office visits, mental health care, maternity care, and some drugs, after federal approval. The law also extends the program’s end date from January 1, 2027, to January 1, 2032.
WA-2025-HB2385.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2385 HBR PL 26, 2026-03-12)

WA-2025-HB2405.s: The law sets up a pilot program for workers who may have posttraumatic stress disorder from their jobs. It lets the state labor department and some self-insurers pay for PTSD evaluation and up to 11 treatment sessions before a claim is decided, with possible extra treatment if a decision takes longer than 90 days. It also allows funding for workplace mental health projects for jobs with high trauma exposure. It takes effect July 1, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2405.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2405-S SBR APS 26, 2026-03-05)

WA-2025-HB2410.s: Creates a Washington State Commercial Truck Safety and Education Council to suggest ways to improve truck safety, training, research, and public education. The council would include state officials, industry members, a public member, and a labor member, and it must meet at least four times a year and report to the Legislature each year. It also raises the commercial vehicle safety enforcement fee from $16 to $32, with the extra money going to a new account for council-recommended safety work.
WA-2025-HB2410.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2410-S HBR PL 26, 2026-03-10)

WA-2025-HB2411.s: This law expands Washington’s shared leave program for state workers. It lets an employee use shared leave if they are a victim of a hate crime or if they miss work because they or a close family or household member is involved in immigration enforcement, like detainment, court proceedings, or deportation. To qualify for the immigration-related leave, the employee must be legally able to work in the United States, and employers may ask for proof but must not require personal immigration details.
WA-2025-HB2411.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2411-S SBR APS 26, 2026-03-05)

WA-2025-HB2416.s: This law changes how waste-to-energy facilities are treated under the climate commitment act. It gives no-cost allowances to certain waste-to-energy facilities built before 1992 from 2027 through 2030 if they meet federal and state air quality rules, and some of those allowances must be sold at auction for projects that reduce greenhouse gas emissions. It also requires the owner or operator of those facilities to submit a two-part plan on emissions reduction, waste reduction, and material recovery. The law also changes rules for how allowances are allocated to electric utilities and how some of those allowances may be used for ratepayer benefits.

WA-2025-HB2418.s: Changes how cities, counties, and some other local and state permit reviewers count review time for project permit applications, especially for residential projects. It says a request is complete when the required forms and materials are in, and that some waiting time, like waiting for a fee to be paid or for another agency to act, does not count toward the review deadline. It also sets a 20% fee refund for certain government reviews that miss the deadline, unless the applicant waives or extends the deadline; the law takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2418.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2418-S2.E SBR LGV TA 26, 2026-02-22)

WA-2025-HB2420.s: The law raises the dollar limit for public works projects that can use the small works roster, which is a simpler way to hire for smaller government projects. Starting after December 31, 2026, the limit increases in steps from $530,000 to $650,000 by July 1, 2030. It became law and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2420.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2420-S SBR APS 26, 2026-03-05)

WA-2025-HB2426.s: The law lets permit appeals to the pollution control hearings board be heard by smaller or different board setups, if everyone involved agrees. Those options can include an administrative appeals judge, some board members with environmental knowledge, or one qualified board member. The change is meant to help use staff and resources more efficiently, and it takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2426.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2426 HBR PL 26, 2026-03-17)

WA-2025-HB2428.s: The law requires insurers to send a written warning at least 30 days before an individual life insurance policy may lapse for missed premium payments, and to keep proof that the notice was delivered. It also lets policyholders name a third person to get a copy of the lapse notice, and insurers must tell applicants about that option. These rules apply to individual life insurance policies issued on or after January 1, 2027, with some policy types left out.
WA-2025-HB2428.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2428-S SBR APS 26, 2026-03-04)

WA-2025-HB2429.s: The law requires the Governor to help state agencies work together on the Washington Thriving Strategic Plan for children and youth behavioral health. It also creates or keeps in place a leadership council and an executive coordination officer to track the plan, help build needed systems, and look at equity impacts. The Children and Youth Behavioral Health Work Group is extended until December 30, 2031, and state, tribal, local, and nonprofit groups working in this area must align with the plan in an equitable way.
WA-2025-HB2429.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2429 HBR APP 26, 2026-02-10)

WA-2025-HB2431.s: Starting with property taxes due for 2027, nonprofit-owned public assembly halls and meeting places could hold more regular fundraising events and still keep their property tax break, up to 50 days a year instead of 15. The bill also exempts this change from some state review steps and from the 10-year end date that can apply to tax breaks. It became law and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2431.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2431 HBR PL 26, 2026-03-10)

WA-2025-HB2436.s: Oil tankers between 40,000 and 125,000 deadweight tons that enter Puget Sound would need at least one tug escort with enough total engine power to meet the larger of 3,000 deadweight tons or 5% of the tanker’s size. The law took effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2436.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2436 HBR PL 26, 2026-03-10)

WA-2025-HB2441.s: This law changes Washington retirement benefits for the surviving spouse or domestic partner of a member killed in the course of employment. It says the retirement allowance may include reimbursement for premiums on employer-provided medical insurance, COBRA, Medicare Part A, Medicare Part B, or other medical insurance, with some limits. It also says the new premium reimbursement rules apply to payments made after June 10, 2010.

WA-2025-HB2442.s: The law lets local governments use some real estate excise tax money to clear nuisance properties. It also lets counties and cities start a 0.01% sales tax in 2027 to pay for added help for children and families, and it expands how some local housing tax money can be used for upkeep, repairs, and rental help. It also changes rules for some property tax lifts, rental car tax money for criminal justice work, and flood recovery aid.
WA-2025-HB2442.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2442-S.E HBR SA 26, 2026-03-09)

WA-2025-HB2445.s: The law changes who can be named to handle an estate after someone dies, and gives the court more time before picking a public guardian, guardian ad litem, or a “suitable person” who is not a lawyer or trust company. It also adds new rules for people who can serve, limits some “suitable person” appointees to two petitions a year, and requires more detail and notice in probate court papers. It takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2445.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2445 HBA CRJ 26, 2026-01-26)

WA-2025-HB2451.s: The law changes how local governments can use tax increment financing, a way to use future tax growth to pay for public improvements in an area. It limits which areas can be included, requires a set end date and construction deadline, and says the public improvements must be needed for the expected private development. It also adds more detail for project reviews and revenue impact checks with affected taxing districts, and it takes effect on June 2, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2451.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2451-S2.E SBR APS 26, 2026-03-05)

WA-2025-HB2452.s: Under the MHLTA, rent increase notices would no longer have to be served the same way as unlawful detainer notices. They would instead be served by hand, or if the tenant is away, by posting a copy on the home and mailing a copy to the tenant's last known address. The bill became law and takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2452.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2452-S HBR PL 26, 2026-03-10)

WA-2025-HB2467.s: A person may drive a fifth-wheel travel trailer on public roads in Washington if it is no more than 46 feet long, measured from the center of the hitch point to the back of the trailer. A fifth-wheel is a camping or travel trailer that has no engine and is attached to the bed of a pickup truck.
WA-2025-HB2467.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2467-S HBR PL 26, 2026-03-10)

WA-2025-HB2471.s: Creates a state process for collective bargaining when federal labor rules no longer cover certain private-sector workers. It lets Washington's labor agency certify bargaining representatives and hold elections or card checks for covered employees and employers. The law takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2471.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2471-S.E SBR LC OC 26, 2026-02-20)

WA-2025-HB2475.s: This law requires the Office of Equity to work with others to make statewide language-access rules for state programs, activities, and services by December 1, 2027. These rules must cover spoken, signed, written, audio, tactile, and visual communication in a person's main language, across in-person, phone, virtual, recorded, paper, and digital use. State agencies must later report how they will carry out the rules and what resources they may need. The Office of Equity must also submit a plan to address shortages of qualified interpreters and translators, including for less common languages and rural areas.
WA-2025-HB2475.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2475-S SBA SGTE 26, 2026-02-19)

WA-2025-HB2479.s: Creates a state account for wage complaint penalties and a new program run by the Labor and Industries department to give early payments to some low-wage workers who are owed pay. To qualify, a worker must have a wage complaint with merit, meet income and harm rules, and give up appeals and private lawsuits tied to that claim. The program can pay up to 85% of expected wages, with a $2,500 cap, and the law takes effect June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2479.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2479-S2 SBA WM 26, 2026-02-27)

WA-2025-HB2487.s: The law changes how the business tax exemption for insurance premium income works for insurers in Washington. It limits that exemption to premiums already taxed under state law, or to premiums earned by insurers that are already exempt from those premium taxes, and it puts related exemptions into one section of the law. The change applies back to October 2, 2019, and the law takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2487.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2487 HBR FIN 26, 2026-02-10)

WA-2025-HB2495.s: In cities with more than 700,000 people, an unattended vehicle left in a streetcar right-of-way can be treated as an unauthorized vehicle and removed right away if it blocks streetcar use or puts public safety at risk. A city representative in one of these cities may ask for the vehicle to be impounded, which means taken away and held.
WA-2025-HB2495.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2495 HBR PL 26, 2026-03-12)

WA-2025-HB2496.s: This law changes how the energy facility site evaluation council consults with federally recognized tribes when an energy facility is proposed in their area. It requires the council to offer government-to-government consultation within 90 days after receiving an application, and to include a summary of that consultation in its report to the governor. It also says that this kind of tribal consultation is not covered by the state open meetings law.

WA-2025-HB2505.s: The law creates an exemption from adult family home licensing for some people who used to care for foster youth. It applies to certain former foster care providers and child-specific license holders if they meet set safety and licensing history rules, and if the only unrelated adults getting care are those former foster youth. It takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2505.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2505-S HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-20)

WA-2025-HB2508.s: The law expands when the Office of Independent Investigations can look into deadly-force cases and deaths tied to other uses of force by a police officer, including some past cases if new evidence comes up. It also changes which agencies must alert the office right away, lets the office request help from an independent investigation team, and gives the office access to more records, with some health information only shared with consent or a court order. It also adds new limits on public release of some investigation records, and it took effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2508.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2508-S.E HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-27)

WA-2025-HB2521.s: The law lets the Washington State Patrol set the fee for firearms background checks at a level that covers the full cost of running the state background check program. It affects people who get these checks and takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2521.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2521 HBR APH 26, 2026-02-23)

WA-2025-HB2523.s: The law changes Washington’s community reinvestment program and requires the state Office of Equity and Commerce, with community groups, to update the reinvestment plan at least every five years starting in 2032. The plan must include funding advice, rules for how money is shared, and ways to track results. It also sets grant rules for certain groups, creates a work group to make a report and transition plan by July 1, 2027, and calls for a state study of how the money is used. The bill became law and took effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2523.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2523-S2.E HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-28)

WA-2025-HB2525.s: Washington State University must set up a heritage orchard program. The program must keep a list of heritage orchards in Washington and a list of rare or lost apple types. A heritage orchard is one with at least five apple trees that are more than 74 years old, or one with at least one rare or lost apple tree type. It became law and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2525.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2525-S SBR APS 26, 2026-03-05)

WA-2025-HB2532.s: This law makes it a gross misdemeanor to sell, give away, distribute, or offer to sell devices or containers that hold nitrous oxide or flavored nitrous oxide, or a chemical compound mixed with nitrous oxide. It does not apply to medical, veterinary, or dental use, food products used as a propellant, manufacturing or industrial use, certain gas distribution, or automotive purposes. The law is effective June 11, 2026.

WA-2025-HB2539.s: This law raises the income limit for when an inmate is counted as indigent to $100. Starting July 1, 2027, the Department of Corrections must post that rate on its website and at each prison where inmates can see it. Starting July 1, 2029, and every four years after that, the department must raise the limit using inflation data, but not lower it.
WA-2025-HB2539.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2539-S HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-27)

WA-2025-HB2548.s: The law expands the kinds of health care deals that must get 60 days' notice, including changes in control, major asset sales, and some nonprofit-to-for-profit conversions. It also requires parties to share ownership details, tell the Attorney General when the deal closes, and wait if more information is requested. The Attorney General must post quarterly public notices, and filing fees apply to these notices based on deal value, with some exceptions.
WA-2025-HB2548.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2548-S.E HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-HB2575.s: Changes several reporting rules for energy and utility programs. It would make some qualifying utilities file Energy Independence Act reports every two years instead of every year, and it changes some wording about renewable energy credits and target compliance. It also ends some reports on utility disconnections during heat alerts and the state’s electricity supply, and it became law.
WA-2025-HB2575.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2575 HBA ENVI 26, 2026-01-23)

WA-2025-HB2588.s: County ferry districts would be allowed to use their powers for ferries in general, not just passenger-only ferries. That includes using tax money and bond financing for ferry work. The 10-mile limit on operating a ferry crossing or bridge near a state-run crossing or toll bridge would not apply to ferry service run by a ferry district. It became law and takes effect June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2588.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2588 HBA LG 26, 2026-01-29)

WA-2025-HB2594.s: This law sets state policy to give homeless children and youths equal access to the same free, appropriate public education as other students. It requires the state superintendent and school districts to review and change policies that create barriers to identification, enrollment, attendance, and school success for homeless students. It also requires schools to enroll these students right away, help with records and immunizations, and provide transportation and other support tied to their school of origin when needed.

WA-2025-HB2604.s: State rules for giving a car to an insurer would allow certain transfer papers to use an electronic signature and to be printed, even without a notary. The Department of Licensing would have to accept a limited power of attorney, which is a form that lets someone act for you, for this kind of transfer. It became law and takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2604.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2604 HBR PL 26, 2026-03-12)

WA-2025-HB2610.s: This law changes a property tax break for nonprofit housing providers. It lets a nonprofit that gets the tax exemption temporarily rent or lend the property to another group without losing the exemption, if certain rules are met. The nonprofit must file a renewal form each year, and the exemption can also continue if the property is moved to another nonprofit that gets a tax break for a different use.
WA-2025-HB2610.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2610 HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-HB2624.s: The law changes consumer rules for some real estate deals. It says certain notice rules do not apply when public groups, federally recognized Indian tribes, or nonprofit land conservancy groups buy land for a public benefit, as long as they have an appraisal before closing. It takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2624.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2624 HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-HB2664.s: The law changes how unlawful detainer notices, which are notices to leave property, can be served. It removes the need for certified mail and lets a notice count as served when it is mailed from inside Washington with the right address and postage. In some cases, it also changes the steps for giving notice to a tenant or other person holding the property, and it takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-HB2664.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (2664 SBR APS 26, 2026-03-05)

WA-2025-HB2681.s: The law raises the yearly license fee for cannabis producers, processors, and retailers from $1,381 to $1,781. Starting July 1, 2027, the state liquor and cannabis board must also add the change in the Seattle area Consumer Price Index to those license fees each year.
WA-2025-HB2681.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2681 HBR APP 26, 2026-02-10)

WA-2025-HB2689.s: Changes Washington’s Working Connections Child Care program. It keeps income eligibility at 60% of the state median income instead of raising it later, sets child care subsidy base rates at the 75th percentile of market rates starting July 1, 2027, and changes how providers can claim subsidy payments based on a child’s attendance. It also bars different subsidy rates within the same subsidy region and became law as Chapter 264, 2026 Laws, effective April 1, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2689.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2689-S HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-HB2711.s: Changes transportation taxes and fees, including fuel taxes, luxury vehicle and boat taxes, and aircraft taxes. It also creates a new state account for money used to support sustainable aviation fuel work at airports. Some aircraft tax and fee increases start on dates in 2026, 2027, and 2028, and the bill became law.
WA-2025-HB2711.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (2711-S.E HBR PL 26, 2026-03-20)

WA-2025-HB2714.s: The law requires the Caseload Forecast Council to make forecasts for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program and Washington’s state Food Assistance Program. These forecasts help track how many people may need food aid. It became law and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-HB2714.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (2714-S HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-SB5068.s: The law lets U.S. citizens and people legally allowed to work in the United States apply for certain public jobs in Washington. These jobs include peace officers, firefighters, city police, county sheriffs, and deputy prosecutors. It became law on March 18, 2026.
WA-2025-SB5068.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (5068 SBR 3RD 26, 2026-01-23)

WA-2025-SB5105.s: The law expands Washington crimes about child sex images to also cover fake or altered images made with digital tools, if the image is obscene, even when the child shown cannot be identified. It also changes some defenses in these cases and says prosecutors do not always have to prove the pictured child really exists. It took effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-SB5105.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (5105-S.E2 HBA CS 26, 2026-02-12)

WA-2025-SB5124.s: The law sets up rules for Medicaid managed care plans to have enough skilled nursing homes and rehab hospitals in their networks for people who need post-acute care. The state health agency must set these network rules by January 1, 2028, and managed care contracts starting on or after July 1, 2028, must follow them. The rules must consider local care, how quickly people can get care, and other federal Medicaid rules, and the agency must get input from hospitals, nursing homes, and health plans at several points.
WA-2025-SB5124.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (5124-S.E SBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-SB5156.s: This law requires the state building code council to set standards for cities and counties to allow passenger elevators in apartment buildings with up to six stories and up to 24 units. The elevators must be minimally sized to meet federal accessibility requirements. It also requires the council to convene a technical advisory group to review elevator safety requirements for small apartment buildings.

WA-2025-SB5185.s: The law changes the rules for some internationally trained doctors who want to practice in Washington. It removes a past exemption for some foreign graduates and sets up a pilot path to full medical license for primary care after supervised work, tests, and other checks. The Washington Medical Commission must also report on the pilot each year; the law takes effect June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-SB5185.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (5185-S SBR HA 26, 2026-03-03)

WA-2025-SB5252.s: Starting with property taxes due for calendar year 2027, the bill removes the one-acre limit on a property tax break for nonprofit public assembly halls and meeting places. It affects nonprofits that own these kinds of buildings and land, and it takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-SB5252.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (5252-S.E HBA FIN 26, 2026-02-12)

WA-2025-SB5272.s: This law makes it a gross misdemeanor to interfere by force or violence, or to intimidate by threat of force or violence, at public or private elementary and secondary schools and at extracurricular athletic activities. It applies to school employees, contractors, students, and officials or volunteers acting as officials at those activities. It also requires schools to notify the public of the penalties for these acts.

WA-2025-SB5292.s: The law changes how Washington sets the paid family and medical leave premium rate. Instead of using a set formula, the Employment Security Department will set the rate each year based on an actuarial report meant to keep the fund solvent and build a four-month reserve by 2030 and after. It became law as Chapter 104, 2026 Laws, and takes effect on January 1, 2028.
WA-2025-SB5292.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (5292-S2 HBA LAWS 26, 2026-02-23)

WA-2025-SB5346.s: The law changes the state’s digital citizenship rules to include mobile devices, which are personal phones or other portable devices used for calls, messages, games, or videos. It directs the state school office to add research and best practices on student mobile device use, and to report by December 15, 2027 on school policies, barriers, recommendations, and student input. School district boards may adopt rules that limit student possession and use of mobile devices during school, and the law took effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-SB5346.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (5346-S SBR FBR 26, 2026-04-16)

WA-2025-SB5395.s: This law changes how health plans handle prior authorization, which is the approval needed before some care or drugs are covered. It requires plans to share more details about the clinician behind a decision, post changes to prior authorization rules in one place on their website, and make some new prior authorization options available online after December 30, 2030. It also says only a licensed doctor or other licensed health worker can make medical necessity decisions, and artificial intelligence cannot be the only way to deny, delay, or change care.
WA-2025-SB5395.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (5395-S2.E SBR HA 26, 2026-03-05)

WA-2025-SB5420.s: This law expands who can qualify for some state veteran and military service benefits in Washington. It adds Space Force Guardians to the state organized militia and includes certain Space Force, NOAA, and U.S. Public Health Service members, plus some military spouses and widows or widowers, in several job, exam, retirement, license, and employment protections. It became Chapter 207, 2026 Laws, and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-SB5420.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (5420 SBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-SB5467.s: The law raises the value limit for water-sewer district property that can be sold without public notice from $2,500 to $5,400. It also raises the limit for water-sewer district real property that can be sold in a private sale from $5,000 to $7,500. It takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-SB5467.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (5467 SBR FBR 26, 2026-03-30)

WA-2025-SB5520.s: The law changes who can seek compensation under the wrongly convicted persons act. It updates what counts as "actually innocent" and adds a rule for new evidence that supports a claim of wrongful conviction. It also changes the facts a person must show when filing a claim and sets new limits for some convictions and jail time. It became law on March 25, 2026, and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-SB5520.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (5520-S HBR APP 26, 2026-03-04)

WA-2025-SB5552.s: This law requires the State Building Code Council to make rules for the building code rules that apply to kit homes by March 31, 2027. Kit homes are small homes, 800 square feet or less, made from prefabricated walls, floors, and roofs put together on site. The council may also later update those rules.
WA-2025-SB5552.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (5552-S.E SBR FBR 26, 2026-03-30)

WA-2025-SB5690.s: This law directs the Washington State Department of Transportation to set rules that give utility owners early notice about planned state highway fish barrier removal projects, when possible at least one year ahead, so they can work with the agency. It also tells the agency to try to get the most federal money possible for projects that can also cover utility moving costs. The agency is encouraged to send certain federal grant or rebate money into the Multimodal Transportation Account and to report any needed changes in state law, rules, or policy to help get that funding more easily.
WA-2025-SB5690.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (5690-S2 SBR FBR 26, 2026-04-06)

WA-2025-SB5720.s: Requires more details and papers before a court can enter a default judgment in a consumer debt case. A consumer must also get a notice that explains what can happen if they do not answer and where to find legal help. It applies to consumer debt cases started on or after January 1, 2027, and became Chapter 107, 2026 Laws.
WA-2025-SB5720.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (5720-S SBR FBR 26, 2026-04-06)

WA-2025-SB5820.s: The law changes planning rules for Clark County and the cities in it. It removes the authority to use special land-use rules for freight rail use near short line railroads and to include that use in the transportation part of the local comprehensive plan. It became law and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-SB5820.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (5820 HBR APH 26, 2026-03-04)

WA-2025-SB5825.s: The Washington State Leadership Board would be allowed to ask for gifts, grants, and endowments from public or private sources. Money from private sources could be used for projects and programs that are not already funded by the Legislature, and the board would have to report those funds to the Office of Financial Management. The law also removes references to an expired sports mentoring program. It became law and takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-SB5825.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (5825-S HBR APH 26, 2026-03-03)

WA-2025-SB5827.s: This law changes the definition of a “qualifying discharge” for Washington’s veterans’ preference program for civil service. It lets some applicants claim veterans’ scoring criteria before discharge if they have a predischarge certification and later provide official discharge paperwork. It also tells agencies how to verify that certification and says it cannot be used for retention or layoff preference unless official discharge documents are provided.

WA-2025-SB5834.s: The law changes how interest from retirement trust funds can be used to pay expenses. It ends a temporary rule and makes it easier to use those earnings for fraud prevention work, like audits, cybersecurity, petition decisions, and work with the Attorney General's Office to help protect the funds from losses. It became law and takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-SB5834.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (5834-S HBR APH 26, 2026-03-04)

WA-2025-SB5837.s: The law changes rules for guardianship and conservatorship. It lowers the age to be appointed from 21 to 18, or to an emancipated minor, and removes a rule that only relatives could avoid a filing fee in some cases. For guardianship of a minor, it speeds up hearings, changes how notice can be given, lets the court use a visitor or lawyer in more cases, and gives minors more chance to take part in the case.
WA-2025-SB5837.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (5837 SBR LAW TA 26, 2026-01-16)

WA-2025-SB5841.s: The law changes Washington’s high school and beyond plan rules to add help with completing postsecondary financial aid applications. The statewide online platform must show students, parents or guardians, and school staff the student’s progress and completion status for state and federal financial aid applications. It must also send yearly reminders to students in the college bound scholarship program to complete the financial aid applications they need for aid, and it may also send those reminders to parents or guardians.

WA-2025-SB5845.s: Beginning January 1, 2027, health carriers and plans for public employees would have to pay or deny clean claims within 30 days. For claims that are not clean, they would have to send notice within 21 days saying the claim is denied with a reason, or asking for the extra information needed to process it. The law also sets payment of interest on claims that miss these timing and notice rules, and it became Chapter 158, 2026 Laws, with an effective date of June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-SB5845.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (5845-S.E SBR FBR 26, 2026-04-13)

WA-2025-SB5847.s: This law changes workers' compensation medical care rules and directs the department to set minimum standards for providers who treat injured workers. It creates a health care provider network, allows some nonnetwork care for an initial office or emergency room visit when the network is in the worker's area, and sets rules for network approval, oversight, and removal. It also creates a second tier of network providers and directs the department to develop incentives and best practices for them. The law applies to injured workers, providers, self-insurers, and the department.

WA-2025-SB5855.s: This law says a law enforcement officer may not wear a facial covering while interacting with the public while doing official duties. It defines facial covering and exempts undercover operations, certain SWAT protective gear, and some required or authorized protective equipment. A person detained in violation of this law may bring a civil action for damages against the officer in the officer’s official capacity.

WA-2025-SB5862.s: The law gives a one-time 3% increase in retirement benefits to certain retirees in the teachers' and public employees' retirement systems. It applies to Plan 1 retirees who were retired on or before July 1, 2025, and who are not getting the minimum benefit, with the increase capped at $110 a month. The change takes effect on July 1, 2026.
WA-2025-SB5862.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (5862-S HBR APP 26, 2026-03-03)

WA-2025-SB5863.s: The law changes when some restricted state records in the State Archives can be opened. Records are open for viewing and copying after 75 years, but records that are still confidential under other privacy laws stay private. It also requires documents and artifacts in the Lakeland Village preservation plan to be kept through 2030.
WA-2025-SB5863.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (5863 SBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-SB5868.s: The law adds one superior court judge in Skagit County and one in Yakima County. Skagit County’s judges go from four to five, and Yakima County’s go from eight to nine. It became law on March 25, 2026, and takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-SB5868.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (5868 SBR FBR 26, 2026-04-16)

WA-2025-SB5872.s: The state created the PreK Promise Account to hold gifts, grants, or donations for the ECEAP early learning program. Money in the account must be used only to support that program. The Department of Children, Youth, and Families must keep track of deposits by each donor, and only the agency secretary may approve spending.
WA-2025-SB5872.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (5872 SBR WM OC 26, 2026-02-04)

WA-2025-SB5874.s: The law lets the Employment Security Department commissioner waive penalties for small reporting mistakes on unemployment tax and wage reports. It includes mistakes from software that fails to list each worker’s job title or job category. It takes effect on June 11, 2026.
WA-2025-SB5874.src: Washington Legislature final bill report (5874-S SBR FBR 26, 2026-03-30)

WA-2025-SB5880.s: The law lets blood or breath tests be done by a lab that is certified or accredited under a forensic testing standard, not just by the Washington State Patrol lab. Cities and counties may use private labs and accept donations to help pay for them, but they do not have to fund private testing. If a city or county uses a private lab, it must pay the State Patrol back for the cost of returning and handling the evidence. The law takes effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-SB5880.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (5880-S2 HBA CS 26, 2026-02-16)

WA-2025-SB5886.s: This law expands personality rights to cover forged digital likenesses, which are fake digital images or audio of a real, identifiable person that can fool a reasonable person. It sets the civil penalty for misuse at $3,000 and makes the person who violated the law pay that penalty plus actual damages, and in these cases also noneconomic damages. The law took effect on 6/11/2026.
WA-2025-SB5886.src: Washington Legislature House bill report (5886-S HBR CRJ 26, 2026-02-27)

WA-2025-SB5890.s: This bill would change Washington law on negligent driving in the first degree. It would make it a misdemeanor for a person to drive more than 30 miles per hour over the posted speed limit while also driving in a negligent way that endangers or is likely to endanger a person or property. If a person has one or more prior convictions for that speed offense, it would be a gross misdemeanor, and some repeat offenders would have to install an ignition interlock device.

WA-2025-SB5892.s: The law tightens rules for who can get records from Washington’s voter registration databases. County election offices must send such requests to the Secretary of State, and some voter info like a driver’s license number, ID card number, Social Security number, and full birthdate is kept private. People who knowingly share protected database information the wrong way can be charged with a class C felony. It took effect on March 25, 2026.
WA-2025-SB5892.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (5892 SBR APS 26, 2026-02-05)

WA-2025-SB5899.s: This bill would create a license endorsement for qualified licensed chiropractors to perform chiropractic diagnosis and adjustments on nonhuman animals. To use the endorsement, a chiropractor must meet training or certification requirements, follow recordkeeping rules, and work from a written referral from a licensed veterinarian who has personally examined the animal. It would also set limits on animal chiropractic care, including no imaging orders, and require a joint task force to review complaints and report to the governor and legislature.

WA-2025-SB5901.s: The bill would change how state school construction aid is calculated for schools on military bases. It would leave those school facilities out of a district’s count of available classroom space and raise the state aid share by 15% for projects on a military base.
WA-2025-SB5901.src: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (5901-S SBR APS 26, 2026-02-17)

WA-2025-SB5904.s:
This bill changes Washington law on who may use nursing titles. It says only licensed registered nurses, advanced registered nurse practitioners, nurse practitioners, and licensed practical nurses may use those titles and abbreviations, and it keeps an exception for people listed as Christian Science nurses if they do not hold themselves out as one of those licensed nurses.

It also sets one version of the law to expire on June 30, 2027, and makes the other version take effect on that date.

WA-2025-SB5905.s: The bill would add two new exceptions to who can join the Public Employees' Retirement System for port district workers. Port workers who are enrolled in a federal railroad retirement plan or a union-sponsored defined benefit retirement plan would not be able to participate in PERS.
